name: Wood Violet
lede: Wood Violet is a deep blue-purple that appears as a color name in a 1930 dictionary and again as a Pantone name, and that also names a woodland flower.

sections.title: A flower and a swatch
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists Wood Violet as a fashion-and-textile name, first recorded in 1922 [1]. Finlay names it among the evocative color names that the Pantone founder Herbert added to his system, alongside moss tone and doe [2]. Baty's book on nature's palette lists wood violet as another name for the sweet violet, *Viola odorata*, in its blues and purples [3].

The swatch is a dark, strongly saturated purple, near [[purple]], [[rebecca-purple]] and [[royal-purple]], about six and a half units from plain purple [4]. The name points to the flower rather than describing the tint of this swatch [3][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, none has a color within six units of this swatch over five per cent of its canvas [5]. The photographs are of aged, varnished paintings, and a dark purple of this strength is rare in them [5]. The page is short because the books say little more than the name and its flower [1][3].
